items.name: Finite patching modules and coefficient power series
items.statement: Define the projected Pontryagin-dual finite modules M_{m,K_p,r}, then adjoin S-frames and quotient augmentation powers to obtain M^square. Choose generators of each auxiliary Delta and maps O[[y_1,...,y_q]] to its group ring. S_infty combines these diamond variables with the frame variables, with fixed augmentation quotient.
items.note: Route owner: CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibilityPartIIPatchedGLdDensity. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Ultrafilter patched module
items.statement: Choose a nonprincipal ultrafilter on the auxiliary levels. The localized product of O modulo varpi^r has completion O; use this to form the inverse limit of the tensor of products of finite patching modules. Its augmentation quotient is completed localized automorphic forms. This choice-dependent construction must precede any later independence theorem.
items.note: Route owner: CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibilityPartIIPatchedGLdDensity. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Projectivity and regular sequence of the patched module
items.statement: The diamond and frame variables form an M_infty-regular sequence. The augmentation quotient is projective over O[[G_0(Z_p)]], giving maximal Cohen–Macaulayness and, by [82, Theorem6.2], finite projectivity over S_infty[[G_0(Z_p)]]. No generic rank-one conclusion follows here.
items.note: Route owner: CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibilityPartIIPatchedGLdDensity. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Patched deformation ring and its actions
items.statement: Form R_infty=R_loc[[x_1,...,x_g]] with g given by the Taylor–Wiles generator bound, choose maps to finite-level framed rings, and obtain its action on M_infty. Formal smoothness lifts the S_infty-action. The printed g uses [F:Q] where PropositionA.3.3 gives [F+:Q]; use the corrected degree [F+:Q] as recorded in E24.
items.note: Route owner: CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibilityPartIIPatchedGLdDensity. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Exact covariant patching functor
items.statement: Set M_infty(W)=Hom_cont,O[[G_0(Z_p)]](M_infty,W^vee)^vee. Projectivity makes it exact and covariant on finite coefficient modules, with finite R_infty- and S_infty-values. For a Serre weight its augmentation quotient identifies with the dual localized automorphic space of dual coefficients.
items.note: Route owner: CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibilityPartIIPatchedGLdDensity. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Support and maximal Cohen–Macaulay properties
items.statement: Local-global compatibility forces type evaluations to factor through the appropriate ordered semistable quotient. Dimension equality gives maximal Cohen–Macaulayness there and, for weight constituents, on its special fiber. Nakayama identifies nonzero patched weight values with modular weights. The away-from-p tensor is equidimensional by [5]/[12], and is not asserted formally smooth for arbitrary level.
items.note: Route owner: CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibilityPartIIPatchedGLdDensity. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Explicit rank-three monodromy chart
items.statement: For n=3, singleton J, lambda=(3,1,0), z=(23)t_(2,1,1), write the universal determinant-bounded chart matrix and impose det(A)=-(v-t)^4, minor divisibility and reduced closure. Central translation reduces the monodromy parameter to (a,b,0).

items.name: Explicit open genericity locus
items.statement: Use V=Spec Z[a,b,1/P] with P=7! b(b-1)(a-1)(a-2)(a-b)(a-b-1)(a-b-2). Invert all these factors before eliminating variables or asserting normality; the coefficient prime therefore exceeds 7.

items.name: Three equations for the explicit chart
items.statement: On V the rank-three chart is presented by the three displayed polynomials in t,a,b,c12,c13,d21,c22,d31,d33, eliminating the other six chart coefficients using monodromy and t-torsion-freeness. The exact three equations are in sourceData.appendixB.chartEquations. Rational-function-field consistency checks are recorded in validation; a uniform localized-integer certificate is a remaining blueprint proof obligation.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Seven special-fiber components
items.statement: On t=0 the chart has the seven component ideals listed in sourceData.appendixB.specialFiberMinimalPrimes. Keep scheme multiplicities distinct from the list of minimal primes; this is not a claim that the original special fiber is reduced.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Complete intersection and flatness of the explicit chart
items.statement: On V the presented chart is an irreducible complete intersection flat over X times V. Fiber codimension three and the regular domain generic fiber identify the presentation with the flat closure.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Effective Elkik Jacobian bound
items.statement: The ideal of 3-by-3 minors of the relative Jacobian of the three-equation presentation contains t^3. The source cites a Macaulay2 computation without a displayed certificate; this needs an independently reproducible polynomial certificate or explicit outstanding proof leaf, not a claimed verified computation.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Partial normalization by an explicit fraction
items.statement: Adjoin W=-t d21/c22 in the fraction field of the chart. The seven displayed relations define the proposed finite birational partial normalization. All statements here are after base change to V, as required by the proposition. The exact seven relations are in sourceData.appendixB.partialNormalizationEquations.

items.name: Normal O-flat specialization
items.statement: For a specialization (-p,a,b) in X times V over O, the chart is O-flat and its specified partial normalization is O-flat and normal, hence the normalization. The proof uses a specialized Groebner basis, Cohen–Macaulay leading ideal, generically reduced special fiber, topological flatness and the Pappas–Zhu normality criterion, with regular generic fiber.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Normalization fibers of all seven components
items.statement: Table1 gives the decomposition of the inverse image of each original component, distinguishing the unique maximal-dimensional component from lower-dimensional extras. All seven rows were read in the rotated PDF image and transcribed in sourceData.appendixB.normalizationFiberComponents. The ideals are in the normalization quotient: row four retains its inherited quadratic W equation.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Unibranch fixed point and a dense branching locus
items.statement: For p>7 and all seven parameter factors units, the chart is unibranch at z because its normalization fiber is a singleton. On the component (c22,c13,c12), a generically étale degree-two normalization cover gives a Zariski-dense locus that is not geometrically unibranch. This disproves a blanket all-point unibranch conclusion; distinguish ordinary from geometric unibranchness at nonclosed points.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Explicit depth-ten local comparison in one chart
items.statement: For n=3,K=Q_p,lambda=(3,1,0),z=(23)t_(2,1,1), a 5-generic presentation with mu 10-deep gives the local comparison conclusions in this chart, using Jacobian exponent 3 and m-6+3>6. Use the explicit 10-depth hypothesis: the printed raw polynomial product_{m=0}^{10}(X-Y-m)(Y-Z-m)(Z-X-m) does not imply it, as E26 shows. Alternatively evaluate a signed wall polynomial at mu+eta. Interpret the local isomorphism on the completed framed chart in Theorem7.3.2, retaining its torus torsors.

items.name: Product extension of the numerical example
items.statement: Products preserve the reduced special-fiber and normalization facts in this example, giving the analogous chart statement for general unramified K/Q_p and corresponding product data. This is not an arbitrary-product preservation theorem for unibranchness without the stated geometric hypotheses.

items.name: Type A equivalued affine Springer fixed points
items.statement: Over C, for the simply connected Type A group with chosen Borel/Iwahori and diagonal regular semisimple s, put gamma=t*s. For w in the fundamental box F of dominant restricted alcoves, let Y_w be the closure of G(C[[t]])wB/B intersect Fl_gamma. Then its T-fixed points are exactly the affine Weyl elements y with y<=w0*w. The GLn central-translation and left/right quotient adapters must be supplied when importing this into LLHLM23; the theorem itself is a characteristic-zero result, and LLHLM23 spreads nonempty intersections to obtain polynomial conditions in characteristic p.
items.locator: Cited input [1], Boixeda Alvarez arXiv:1910.04780v3 Theorem3.1, PDF5; definitions PDF1–4; used in LLHLM23 Proposition4.7.3.

items.name: Explicit affine Springer component matrix and inverse
items.statement: For w in the Type A fundamental box, set a^w_ji to the least k for which w^-1(e_i-e_j)+k*delta is a positive affine root. Construct the lower unitriangular matrix whose ji entry is the sum over increasing paths i=i1<...<ik=j of product_l ((s_il-s_i(l+1))/(s_il-s_ik))*t^(sum_l a^w_i(l+1),il)*product_l A_i(l+1),il. Distinct s_i make all denominators units. The inverse has path coefficient (-1)^(k-1)*product_l (s_il-s_i(l+1))/(s_i1-s_i(l+1)). This gives an affine open in the component and satisfies M^-1*t*s*M in w Lie(B). The fixed-point witness reduces to nonsingular determinant minors; the source degree-maximization algorithm and Vandermonde reductions are explicit further proof leaves, with transversality intersection zero.
items.locator: Cited input [1], Boixeda Alvarez arXiv:1910.04780v3 AppendixB.2–B.5, PDF8–17; corrected E29–E31.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Elkik's presentation-dependent Jacobian ideal
items.statement: For B=A[X_1,…,X_N]/J with fixed generators f_1,…,f_q, for each subset α of the generators let F_α be their ideal, Δ_α the ideal of |α|×|α| minors of their Jacobian (zero if |α|>N), and K_α=(F_α:J). Put H=Σ_α K_αΔ_α, with the usual empty-minor convention. Elkik permits a chosen H_B⊂H. The vanishing locus of the image of H in B is the nonsmooth locus.

items.name: Torsionfree complete approximation without a Noetherian test ring
items.statement: For a t-adically complete and separated t-torsionfree ring A, a finite polynomial presentation and admissible H_B, if t^r∈H_B(a), J(a)⊂t^m A and m>2r, there is an exact zero a^0 with a^0−a∈(t^(m−r)A)^N.
items.locator: Proof extracted from Elkik Lemma1 with I=A; used in LLHLM23 Proposition3.3.9
items.note: Continuation by Codex — codex-hjdg0j. Owner: SchemeAndStackFoundations. Planning only.

items.name: A fixed smooth generic presentation gives a uniform exponent
items.statement: For the fixed finitely presented universal chart over the Noetherian base S in U24, smoothness after inverting v implies v^r∈H+J for some r≥0. Choose H_B after base change to be the image of this full universal H, which is admissible by Z03. After any base map S→A with v↦t, an approximate zero modulo t^m with m>r satisfies t^r∈H_B(a) if A is t-adically complete.
items.note: Continuation by Codex — codex-hjdg0j. Owner: SchemeAndStackFoundations. Planning only.

items.name: Geometric connectedness in the affinoid finite-extension sense
items.statement: For a nonzero strict affinoid algebra A over a complete nontrivially valued nonarchimedean field K, call A geometrically connected in the finite-extension sense if Spec(A⊗_K L) is connected for every finite field extension L/K. Z53 identifies each such tensor with the completed tensor. Comparison with the scheme predicate testing arbitrary extensions is a separate interface.
items.note: Continuation by Codex — codex-hjdg0j. Owner: AdicSpacesPartII. Planning only.

api.name: AffinoidGeometricallyConnected.baseChange
api.statement: A finite scalar extension preserves the finite-extension connectedness condition.

api.name: AffinoidGeometricallyConnected.cofinal
api.statement: It suffices to test a cofinal collection of finite field extensions; connectedness descends along further field extension.

api.name: AffinoidGeometricallyConnected.noIdempotents
api.statement: For every finite extension, idempotents are only zero and one.

api.name: AffinoidGeometricallyConnected.completedTensor
api.statement: The completed tensor product preserves this condition once the affinoid fiber comparison is established.

uses.where: U43/Z13 and LLHLM23 Theorem3.7.1 final paragraph
uses.how: The product's connectedness, together with its independently supplied regularity, proves it is a domain.

items.name: BLGGT geometric connectedness of an affinoid product
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_l and A_1,A_2 geometrically connected affinoid K-algebras in the finite-extension sense. Then A_1 completed-tensor_K A_2 is geometrically connected.
items.locator: BLGGT LemmaA.1.1, printed p. 596/PDF96; standing field convention p. 595
items.note: Continuation by Codex — codex-hjdg0j. Owner: AdicSpacesPartII. Planning only.

items.name: A connected affinoid with a rational point is geometrically connected
items.statement: For a complete nontrivially valued nonarchimedean field K, a connected strict affinoid K-algebra A admitting a K-algebra retraction A→K is geometrically connected in the finite-extension sense. Normality and regularity are unnecessary for this conclusion.
items.locator: Implicit input before BLGGT LemmaA.1.1 is applied in LLHLM23 Theorem3.7.1, PDF79–80
items.note: AdicSpacesPartII:R0 affinoid adapter of the general algebraic result Z47. This strengthens the earlier correct normal-connected statement; it is not a new source erratum.

items.name: Khare–Wintenberger completed tensor theorem in its original scope
items.statement: Let O be the integers of a finite extension E/Q_p and R_i a finite family of complete Noetherian local O-algebras with residue field O/m_O. Suppose each R_i is a domain with an O-algebra retraction R_i→O and R_i[1/p] is regular. Their completed tensor product, completed for the sum of maximal ideals, is a domain, has an O-point, and has regular generic fiber.
items.locator: Khare–Wintenberger II Proposition2.2(ii), author PDF9; conventions PDF4–6
items.note: Continuation by Codex — codex-hjdg0j. Owner: DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra. Planning only.

items.name: Domain part over an arbitrary complete DVR
items.statement: Let O be a complete DVR with fraction field K, and R_i complete Noetherian local O-domains with the same residue field as O and O-algebra retractions ξ_i. Assume the local rings of R_i[1/π] at ker(ξ_i)[1/π] are regular. Then the completed tensor over O, for the sum of maximal ideals, is a domain and has an O-point.
items.locator: LLHLM23 Theorem3.7.1, PDF79, general-DVR adaptation of KWII Proposition2.2
items.note: Continuation by Codex — codex-hjdg0j. Owner: DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra. Planning only.

items.name: The chart's completed affinoid product is a domain
items.statement: Let O be the complete DVR R′ used in Theorem3.7.1, π its uniformizer, K its fraction field, and B_j the finite-type flat chart O-algebras. Assume each C_j=π-adic completion of B_j has regular domain generic fiber with a K-point, and each B_j[1/π] is smooth over K as supplied by the generic chart construction. Then C=π-adic completion of ⊗_O B_j is an integral domain.
items.note: AdicSpacesPartII:R0/F0. The finite-type presentation is essential for the flat completion proof. Z57–Z59/Z62 record the remaining regularity-source obligations explicitly.

items.name: Affinoid product connectedness over complete nonarchimedean fields
items.statement: For a complete nontrivially valued nonarchimedean field K and geometrically connected strict K-affinoid algebras A,B in the finite-extension sense, A⊗̂_K B is geometrically connected. No perfection or characteristic-zero assumption on K is imposed.
items.locator: General-field adaptation of BLGGT LemmaA.1.1 used in LLHLM23 Theorem3.7.1, PDF79–80
items.note: Existing AdicSpacesPartII:R0 owner. The stated generality now explicitly matches the nontrivial absolute-value and strict-affinoid conventions of the sources. Generalized radii or trivially valued analytic categories are not inferred from this proof.

items.name: Connected prime spectra via idempotents
items.statement: For a nontrivial commutative ring R, Spec(R) is connected if and only if every idempotent is zero or one.
items.note: Actual declaration read at f790474. Use in U42 and the affinoid finite-extension connectedness API.

items.name: Geometric connectedness of the ordinary algebraic tensor product
items.statement: For commutative K-algebras S,T over a field K, if their spectra are geometrically connected over K in the scheme sense, so is Spec(S⊗_K T).
items.note: Actual declaration read at f790474. This is the ORDINARY tensor product; it is not the completed affinoid product theorem Z09/Z14.

items.name: Krull separation for finite local modules
items.statement: If R is Noetherian local, M is a finite R-module and I is a proper ideal of R, then M is I-adically separated.
items.locator: Mathlib/RingTheory/AdicCompletion/Noetherian.lean:26; Mathlib/RingTheory/Filtration.lean:431 (ring-valued intersection form), reread at the full pin.
items.note: Read at 082e2d3. Apply to quotients M/N to prove closedness, and to the rational-point local ring to prove injectivity into its completion.

items.name: Finite torsionfree modules over a PID are free
items.statement: For a principal ideal domain O and finite torsionfree O-module M, M has a finite basis.
items.note: Read with the inherited domain and principal-ideal hypotheses; applies to a DVR, not an arbitrary valuation ring.

items.name: Continuous evaluation of multivariate power series
items.statement: For commutative rings R,S, a continuous coefficient map into a complete Hausdorff uniform topological ring S with linear topology, and a family satisfying MvPowerSeries.HasEval, evaluation defines a continuous ring homomorphism. It is uniquely specified by its values on polynomials.
items.note: Read actual declarations and standing topological hypotheses. For finitely many variables in a maximal ideal, verify HasEval in the adic topology; a presentation or regular-structure isomorphism does not follow merely from this evaluation API.

items.name: Exactness of completion on finite modules
items.statement: If R is Noetherian, I is an ideal and 0→M→N→P→0 is exact with N finite, I-adic completion preserves exactness.
items.note: Read at 082e2d3. This applies over a Noetherian presentation ring; do not apply it to an unproved Noetherian ordinary tensor of two formal power-series rings.

items.name: Finite-module completion as scalar extension
items.statement: For a Noetherian ring R, ideal I and finite R-module M, the natural map R̂⊗_R M→M̂ is an isomorphism.
items.note: Read at 082e2d3. Together with R≅R̂ this makes a finite module over a complete Noetherian ring complete. It does not commute localization with an arbitrary inverse limit.

items.name: Saturated jets at a DVR-valued point
items.statement: Let O be a complete DVR with uniformizer π, fraction field K, and ξ:R→O a local O-algebra retraction from a complete Noetherian local O-algebra with residue field k_O. Put P=ker ξ, A=R[1/π], q=P A, J_n=(q^n)∩R and Q_n=R/J_n for n≥1. Equivalently J_n={x | ∃a≥0, π^a x∈P^n}.
items.locator: KWII Proposition2.2(ii), author PDF9; explicit proof refinement for LLHLM23 Theorem3.7.1, published PDF79
items.note: Owner DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.1. Uses ordinary ideal localization/comap, not a new saturation carrier.

api.name: SaturatedPointJet.ideal
api.statement: Form q^n and contract along R→R[1/π]; identify membership with some π-power multiple in P^n.

api.name: SaturatedPointJet.transition
api.statement: For m≤n construct Q_n→Q_m from J_n⊂J_m; prove identity and composition, compatibility of augmentations to O, and J_1=P.

api.name: SaturatedPointJet.torsionFree
api.statement: Multiplication by π on Q_n is injective, by saturation; combine with DVR factorization for torsionfreeness.

api.name: SaturatedPointJet.map
api.statement: A local O-algebra map commuting with the chosen retractions carries J_n into J_n and induces a compatible map of quotient systems. No arbitrary base-change equality is asserted.

api.name: SaturatedPointJet.genericFiber
api.statement: Construct the canonical Q_n⊗_O K ≅ A/q^n, compatible in n; see Z18.

api.name: SaturatedPointJet.free
api.statement: Under the given Noetherian hypotheses Q_n is finite free over O by Z17; do not choose bases functorially.

uses.how: These finite free quotients separate the integral completed tensor before passage to the formal generic-point product.

items.name: Chevalley cofinality for complete local modules
items.statement: Let (R,m) be complete Noetherian local, M finite, and N_n a descending sequence of submodules with intersection zero. For every q≥1 there exists n such that N_n⊂m^q M.
items.locator: KWII Proposition2.2(ii), author PDF9; explicit proof refinement for LLHLM23 Theorem3.7.1, published PDF79; proof supplied here by stabilization of finite-length images
items.note: Owner DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.1. Standard Chevalley lemma used by KWII; the Zariski–Samuel book cited there has not been separately read. The complete proof above is an explicit reconstruction, not a quotation or attribution of this proof to that book.

items.name: Saturated point jets are finite free
items.statement: In Z15, each Q_n is a nonzero finite free O-module, its augmentation ideal is nilpotent of exponent at most n, and its maximal-ideal and π-adic topologies agree.
items.locator: KWII Proposition2.2(ii), author PDF9; explicit proof refinement for LLHLM23 Theorem3.7.1, published PDF79

items.name: Generic jets equal the rational local jets
items.statement: With Z15 notation, Q_n⊗_O K ≅ A/q^n ≅ A_q/(qA_q)^n. These canonical isomorphisms commute with the transition maps and with the augmentation to K.
items.locator: KWII Proposition2.2(ii), author PDF9; explicit proof refinement for LLHLM23 Theorem3.7.1, published PDF79

items.name: Regularity survives completion at a rational point
items.statement: For a Noetherian regular local K-algebra B whose residue map identifies B/m with the given field K, its m-adic completion is Noetherian regular local, has residue field K via that same coefficient map, and has dimension dim B.
items.locator: Stacks 15.44.4 (07NY), 15.44.1 and completion facts in 10.97; applied in KWII PDF9
items.note: Reclassified from missing to planned after reading the exact existing ModularCurves §4D target and AUDIT-12/AUDIT-17 overlap evidence. Import only the local completion/regularity atom, not the modular-curve construction or the entire stage's application dependencies. R03.1 consumes it; it must not be planned there a second time.

items.name: Power-series coordinates with a specified coefficient field
items.statement: If B is a complete Noetherian regular local K-algebra and K→B/m is an isomorphism, and b_1,…,b_d lift a K-basis of m/m², then evaluation induces a continuous K-algebra isomorphism K[[X_1,…,X_d]]≅B sending X_i to b_i.
items.locator: Stacks 10.160.10(2), tag 0C0S; applied in KWII PDF9
items.note: R03.1 coefficient-preserving coordinate adapter. Exact Noetherianity, variable-adic completeness, Nakayama, surjectivity and dimension-drop suppliers are now exposed in L13–L23 and Z26–Z29. No arbitrary coefficient-field choice or perfection assumption. Formalization is still missing.

items.name: Complete local tensor product and presentation
items.statement: For a finite family of complete Noetherian local O-algebras with fixed residue field k_O, form C=completed_tensor_O R_i in the topology of the sum of maximal ideals. Choosing finite power-series presentations gives C≅O[[all variables]]/(all presentation relations), so C is Noetherian complete local with residue k_O; its continuous O-algebra maps are the compatible families of maps from the factors.
items.note: Existing R03.1 explicitly plans this construction, Noetherianity and locality. Reuse the AdicSpacesPartII:R0 general topological tensor carrier where its hypotheses fit; the coefficient-category presentation and theorem are the R03.1 adapter, not a second carrier. The finite-power-series presentation, once constructed, imports L13 and L21 for Noetherianity; topology/completeness uses L14/L22 with the actual ideal comparison. Do not infer Noetherianity of the ordinary tensor. The presentation and coefficient-category universal property themselves remain planned, not library.

api.name: CompleteLocalTensor.factorMap
api.statement: Provide continuous local O-algebra maps R_i→C, commuting with the specified residue-field identifications.

api.name: CompleteLocalTensor.homEquiv
api.statement: For a complete Noetherian local O-algebra A with the specified residue field, continuous local O-algebra maps C→A correspond to families of such maps R_i→A; prove evaluation on each factor and uniqueness.

api.name: CompleteLocalTensor.presentation
api.statement: Given finite continuous presentations R_i=O[[X_i]]/I_i, identify C with O[[all X_i]]/(images of I_i); prove independence of the presentations via homEquiv.

api.name: CompleteLocalTensor.quotient
api.statement: For closed ideals J_i in the factors, compare C/(sum J_i C) with the completed tensor of R_i/J_i using quotient maps; Z20 separately identifies its finite-free jet target with an ordinary tensor.

api.name: CompleteLocalTensor.augmentation
api.statement: A family of continuous local O-algebra retractions R_i→O induces C→O whose composite with O→C is identity; do not assume every coefficient algebra has such a retraction.

api.name: CompleteLocalTensor.reindex
api.statement: Reindexing and regrouping finite factors give canonical continuous O-algebra equivalences determined by all factor maps; the empty tensor is O.

uses.how: Extend the factor jet maps to the complete tensor and identify the quotient kernel.
Construct the tensor of the coefficient retractions C→O, ensuring C is nonzero.
Model the completed local ring of a finite product of pointed local models.

items.name: Integral tensor jets are exact quotients
items.statement: For a family indexed by a nonempty finite set of cardinality h, with Z15 hypotheses, let C be Z24, H_n=Σ_i J_(i,n)C and D_n=⊗_O,i Q_(i,n). Then C/H_n≅D_n canonically. Each D_n is finite free and π-adically complete; its augmentation ideal has exponent at most h(n−1)+1.
items.locator: KWII Proposition2.2(ii), author PDF9; explicit proof refinement for LLHLM23 Theorem3.7.1, published PDF79

items.name: The inverse limit of generic box jets
items.statement: For the family in Z20, suppose the local K-algebras (R_i[1/π])_(q_i) are regular of dimensions d_i. Then lim_n(D_n⊗_O K) is (noncanonically after choosing parameters) K[[X_(i,j) | 1≤j≤d_i]].
items.locator: KWII Proposition2.2(ii), author PDF9; explicit proof refinement for LLHLM23 Theorem3.7.1, published PDF79

items.name: The integral completed tensor embeds in generic point jets
items.statement: In Z20, assume each R_i is a domain. The compatible maps C→D_n→D_n⊗_O K define an injective map C→lim_n(D_n⊗_O K).
items.locator: KWII Proposition2.2(ii), author PDF9; explicit proof refinement for LLHLM23 Theorem3.7.1, published PDF79

items.name: The maximal ideal of a local completion
items.statement: For a Noetherian local ring R, its maximal-ideal completion is local and its maximal ideal is the extension of m_R.
items.note: Actual declaration and standing hypotheses read. Locality is the preceding instance; this does not establish Noetherianity of the completion.

items.name: Residue-field invariance under completion
items.statement: For Noetherian local R, the residue-field map induced by R→Rhat is bijective.
items.note: Actual declaration and standing hypotheses read. Preserves the specified coefficient-field map in Z23.

items.name: Embedding dimension is unchanged by completion
items.statement: For Noetherian local R, spanFinrank of the maximal ideal of Rhat equals spanFinrank of m_R.
items.note: Actual declaration and standing hypotheses read. The proof constructs the cotangent comparison; cite the exported rank equality, not a fabricated named cotangent equivalence.

items.name: Adic completion is flat
items.statement: For a Noetherian commutative ring R and any ideal I, AdicCompletion I R is flat as an R-module.
items.note: Actual declaration and standing hypotheses read. No Noetherianity of the completed ring is concluded by flatness.

items.name: Prime-height formula for a going-down map
items.statement: Let R,S be Noetherian commutative rings, S an R-algebra satisfying going-down, p a prime of R and P a prime of S lying over p. Then ht(P)=ht(p)+ht(P mod pS).
items.note: Actual declaration and standing hypotheses read. Flatness supplies Algebra.HasGoingDown.of_flat at Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/GoingDown.lean:154 (read). Both rings must be Noetherian; this cannot prove Noetherianity of completion.

items.name: Finite-variable power series over a Noetherian ring are Noetherian
items.statement: For finite sigma and Noetherian commutative R, MvPowerSeries sigma R is Noetherian.
items.note: Actual declaration and standing hypotheses read. The proof uses finSuccEquiv and the one-variable theorem; no completion-Noetherianity assumption.

items.name: Variable-adic completeness of finite-variable power series
items.statement: For finite sigma and any commutative R, R[[X_sigma]] is complete and separated for the ideal generated by its variables.
items.note: Actual declaration and standing hypotheses read. The directly applicable anonymous instance at lines213–222 was read; no invented instance name. Its proof transports completeness along the named equivalence from Equiv.lean:344.

items.name: Surjectivity from a residue quotient
items.statement: For a ring homomorphism f:A→B and ideal J⊆A, if A is J-adically precomplete, B is J.map(f)-adically separated, and A→B/J.map(f) is surjective, then f is surjective.
items.note: Actual declaration and standing hypotheses read. There is no finiteness or Noetherianity hypothesis. Identify the mapped ideal before applying it.

items.name: A non-zero-divisor kernel lowers dimension
items.statement: If f:R→S is surjective and its kernel contains a non-zero-divisor r, then dim(S)+1≤dim(R).
items.note: Actual declaration and standing hypotheses read. For a power-series domain over a field, any nonzero kernel element qualifies. The +1 argument uses the finite dimension supplied by Z27.

items.name: One extra formal variable raises dimension at least one
items.statement: For any commutative ring R, dim(R)+1≤dim(R[[X]]).
items.note: Actual declaration and standing hypotheses read. Only a lower bound. Iteration uses MvPowerSeries.finSuccEquiv at Equiv.lean:170; no upper-bound theorem is claimed.

items.name: Local dimension is bounded by generators of the maximal ideal
items.statement: For a Noetherian local ring R, ringKrullDim R≤spanFinrank(m_R).
items.note: Actual declaration and standing hypotheses read. Combines with an explicit finite-variable maximal-ideal calculation in Z26.

items.name: The existing regular-local-ring criterion
items.statement: For Noetherian local R, IsRegularLocalRing R iff spanFinrank(m_R)=ringKrullDim R; equivalently the residue-field dimension of m_R/m_R² equals dim R.
items.note: Actual declaration and standing hypotheses read. Reuse this predicate. The class includes Noetherianity; an equality of dimensions alone does not discharge that instance.

items.name: Power-series units are detected by the constant term
items.statement: A multivariate power series over a ring is a unit iff its constant coefficient is a unit.
items.note: Actual declaration and standing hypotheses read. The following instance gives locality over a local coefficient ring. Over a field the nonunits are exactly zero-constant series.

items.name: Surjective images of Noetherian rings are Noetherian
items.statement: For a surjective ring homomorphism A→B from a Noetherian ring, B is Noetherian.
items.note: Actual declaration and standing hypotheses read. Used only after constructing actual surjectivity of the power-series evaluation.

items.name: Finite-ideal completion and its first quotient
items.statement: For finitely generated I⊆R, Rhat is complete for I Rhat and the surjection evalOne:Rhat→R/I has kernel I Rhat.
items.note: Actual declaration and standing hypotheses read. The kernel lemma is at line198; evalOne surjectivity is Algebra.lean:193. Completeness for the mapped ideal uses LocalRing.lean:isAdicComplete_self. These are available without claiming completion Noetherianity.

items.name: Finite-module Nakayama span criterion
items.statement: For a finite module M over a local ring R and a submodule N, the image of N in M/m_R M is the whole quotient iff N=M.
items.note: Apply to M=m_R, not M=R, to turn lifts of a cotangent basis into generators of m_R.

items.name: Noetherianity of adic completion via a power-series quotient
items.statement: For any ideal I of a Noetherian commutative ring R, the I-adic completion Rhat is Noetherian.
items.locator: Stacks 0316 direct proof; its omitted surjectivity details supplied using pinned L14/L15/L22
items.note: Codex — codex-a71f92. Mathematical proof and exact library contracts supplied; no Lean implementation or independent review claimed. Reuse existing R03.1 infrastructure.

items.name: Finite-variable ideal powers by coefficient vanishing
items.statement: For finite sigma, a commutative ring R, S=R[[X_sigma]], J=(X_i), and n≥0, J^n is exactly the set of series whose coefficients of every monomial of total degree <n vanish.
items.locator: Worker-supplied supplier decomposition for KWII Proposition2.2(ii), LLHLM23 PDF79; source comparisons recorded in continuation report
items.note: Codex — codex-a71f92. Mathematical proof and exact library contracts supplied; no Lean implementation or independent review claimed. Reuse existing R03.1 infrastructure.

items.name: Dimension of finite-variable formal power series over a field
items.statement: For a field K and a finite index set sigma of cardinality d, ringKrullDim(K[[X_sigma]])=d.
items.locator: Worker-supplied supplier decomposition for KWII Proposition2.2(ii), LLHLM23 PDF79; source comparisons recorded in continuation report
items.note: Codex — codex-a71f92. Mathematical proof and exact library contracts supplied; no Lean implementation or independent review claimed. Reuse existing R03.1 infrastructure.

items.name: Dimension is unchanged by local completion
items.statement: For a Noetherian local ring R with maximal ideal m, dim(Rhat)=dim(R) for its m-adic completion.
items.locator: Stacks 07NV (alternative dimension-formula proof); existing ModularCurves §4D target
items.note: Import the existing upstream preservation-of-dimension target, not a parallel R03.1 target. L12 identifies the exact available generic formula; the Noetherian prerequisite is Z25. The upstream local-commutative-algebra atom precedes all modular-curve application layers.

items.name: Generator evaluation surjects with a specified coefficient field
items.statement: Let B be a complete separated local K-algebra, K a field, such that K→B/m is an isomorphism. If b_1,…,b_r generate m as an ideal, then the continuous K-algebra evaluation K[[X_1,…,X_r]]→B, X_i↦b_i, is surjective.
items.locator: Worker-supplied supplier decomposition for KWII Proposition2.2(ii), LLHLM23 PDF79; source comparisons recorded in continuation report
items.note: Codex — codex-a71f92. Mathematical proof and exact library contracts supplied; no Lean implementation or independent review claimed. Reuse existing R03.1 infrastructure.

items.name: Leibniz rule for formal partial derivatives
items.statement: Over a commutative semiring R, for multivariate polynomials f,g and a variable i, ∂_i(fg)=(∂_i f)g+f(∂_i g).
items.note: The derivative is the bundled algebraic derivation MvPolynomial.pderiv. No analytic differentiability or characteristic-zero hypothesis.

items.name: Partial derivative of a multivariate monomial
items.statement: Over a commutative semiring R, ∂_i(a X^s)=a s_i X^(s−e_i), with truncated subtraction and coefficient zero when s_i=0.
items.note: Supplies the formal coefficient in the first-order polynomial expansion over every characteristic.

items.name: Adjugate identity over a commutative ring
items.statement: For a finite square matrix M over a commutative ring, M adj(M)=det(M)·1. No invertibility or non-zero-divisor assumption on det(M) is required.
items.note: Use the existing Matrix.adjugate and finite selected submatrix. The determinant may vanish; no matrix inverse is taken.

items.name: Adic precompleteness gives a congruence limit
items.statement: For a commutative ring R, ideal I and R-module M with IsPrecomplete I M, a sequence f satisfying f_m≡f_n modulo I^m M whenever m≤n has a limit L with f_n≡L modulo I^n M for every n.
items.note: Use M=R coordinatewise. The strengthened tail precision in Z37 is an adapter, not part of this exact declaration.

items.name: Adic separatedness detects zero
items.statement: For an R-module M with IsHausdorff I M, an element whose image modulo I^n M is zero for every n is zero.
items.note: No Noetherian, finite-module or topological continuity assumption.

items.name: An adic ideal in a complete ring lies in the Jacobson radical
items.statement: For a commutative ring R and ideal I, IsAdicComplete I R implies I⊂Jac(R).
items.note: The declaration is in namespace IsAdicComplete; it proves the geometric-series argument without Noetherianity.

items.name: Elements congruent to one modulo the Jacobson radical are units
items.statement: For a commutative ring R, if u−1∈Jac(R), then u is a unit.
items.note: Together with L29, makes 1+t^e b a unit when e≥1 in a (t)-adically complete ring.

items.name: Partial derivatives commute with coefficient base change
items.statement: For a map φ:R→S of commutative semirings and a multivariate polynomial f, ∂_i(map φ f)=map φ (∂_i f).
items.note: Supplies the Jacobian-entry comparison in Z39; conductors require an inclusion argument of their own.

items.name: Algebraic and topological adic completeness agree
items.statement: For a commutative ring R with a uniform structure making its additive group uniform, and a topology that is I-adic, IsAdicComplete I R is equivalent to CompleteSpace R and T2Space R.
items.note: Use the adic uniform structure on the test ring. Completeness alone without separatedness is not the right-hand side.

items.name: Powers preserve injectivity of multiplication
items.statement: In a monoid, if multiplication on the left by t is injective, then multiplication on the left by t^r is injective for every natural r.
items.note: In a commutative ring this discharges cancellation of t^r from an equality; it does not assert cancellation of ideals in a ring with t-torsion.

items.name: First-order polynomial expansion modulo the square of an ideal
items.statement: Let A be a commutative ring, L an ideal, f∈A[X_1,…,X_N], a∈A^N and y∈L^N. Then f(a−y)−f(a)+Σ_i (∂_i f)(a)y_i belongs to L². In particular, y∈(t^s A)^N gives a remainder in t^(2s)A. There is no division by factorials.
items.note: Owner: SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4. Codex — codex-hjdg0j; mathematical proof adapter, no Lean implementation.

items.name: Differentiated conductor relations
items.statement: Let f=(f_1,…,f_q) over a commutative ring A, choose a subset α of p equations, and suppose k f_l=Σ_i c_li f_{α_i} as polynomial identities for all l. Put D_li=∂_i f_l and D_α for its selected rows. The entries of kD−C D_α belong to J=(f_1,…,f_q). Thus if all f_l(a)∈L, then k(a)D(a)−C(a)D_α(a) has entries in L.

items.name: Conductor-weighted minor gives a Jacobian image modulo squared error
items.statement: In Z31, choose p distinct columns β and put M=D_{α,β}(a), δ=det M. Suppose f_l(a)∈L for every l. Define z supported on β by z_β=k(a) adj(M) f_α(a), with all other coordinates zero. Then z∈L^N and k(a)δ f(a)−D(a)z∈(L²)^q. For p=0 use det(0×0)=1, kJ=0 and z=0; the same conclusion holds.

items.name: Jacobian power witness yields a linear correction with controlled precision
items.statement: Let A be a commutative ring in which multiplication by t is injective. With J,H_B as in Z03, suppose J(a)⊂t^m A, t^r∈H_B(a) and m≥r. Then there exists y∈(t^(m−r)A)^N such that f(a)−D(a)y∈(t^(2m−r)A)^q.

items.name: Polynomial evaluation preserves congruences of tuples
items.statement: For a commutative ring A, an ideal L and a,b∈A^N with b_i−a_i∈L for all i, every polynomial f satisfies f(b)−f(a)∈L. Hence for any polynomial ideal H, H(a)+L=H(b)+L, where H(a) is its image ideal under evaluation.

items.name: Persistence of an evaluated ideal power witness
items.statement: Let A be a commutative (t)-adically complete and separated ring, H⊂A[X_1,…,X_N] any ideal, t^r∈H(a), and b−a∈(t^s A)^N with s>r. Then t^r∈H(b). No torsionfreeness or finite generation of H is needed.

items.name: A Newton sequence with a persistent witness and explicit error orders
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Z06 with initial tuple a_0 and m_0>2r, there exists a sequence a_j with m_j=2r+2^j(m_0−2r), f(a_j)∈(t^m_j A)^q, t^r∈H_B(a_j), and a_(j+1)−a_j∈(t^(m_j−r)A)^N for every j. No canonical choice or uniqueness of this sequence is asserted.

items.name: Adic limits retain the full tail precision
items.statement: Let A be a commutative ring with IsAdicComplete I A. Let e_j be a strictly increasing sequence of natural numbers, and let a_j∈A^N satisfy a_(j+1)−a_j∈(I^e_j)^N. There is a unique a_∞ such that a_∞−a_j∈(I^e_j)^N for every j.

items.name: Polynomial equations vanish at a cofinal congruence limit
items.statement: Let A be a commutative ring with IsHausdorff I A, e_j a strictly increasing sequence, and a_j,a_∞∈A^N with a_∞−a_j∈(I^e_j)^N. If f_l(a_j)∈I^m_j for all l,j and m_j≥e_j, then every f_l(a_∞)=0.

items.name: Admissible Elkik ideals survive coefficient base change
items.statement: For a map A→A′ of commutative rings, fix f_1,…,f_q∈A[X_1,…,X_N] and their coefficient images f′. If H_B⊂Σ_α ((f_α):J)Δ_α, then the ideal generated by its image in A′[X] is contained in Σ_α ((f′_α):J′)Δ′_α. This is an inclusion, with no flatness assumption.

items.name: Formal smoothness as a split conormal injection
items.statement: For a surjective R-algebra extension P→B with P formally smooth over R, B is formally smooth over R if and only if its conormal differential J/J²→B⊗_P Ω_(P/R) admits a B-linear left inverse.
items.note: Read with commutative-ring and formally-smooth ambient-algebra hypotheses. Apply to P_Q→B_p, not by assuming B_p has finite presentation over R.

items.name: A spanning family of a finitely presented flat local module contains a basis
items.statement: Over a commutative local ring R, for a finitely presented flat R-module M and a family v_i spanning M, there exist an index type κ, a map a:κ→ι and a basis b of M with b_j=v_(a(j)).
items.note: Z41 first applies this to the conormal module, then to the columns of the transposed split injection. The basis is finite for finite M; its injectivity makes the selected indices distinct.

items.name: Nakayama removes the conormal-square error
items.statement: For submodules N,N′ of a module over a commutative ring, if N′ is finitely generated, I⊂Jac(R), and N′⊂N+I N′, then N′⊂N.
items.note: Apply in P_Q with N=F_alpha P_Q, N′=J P_Q and I=J P_Q. The ideal I is contained in the maximal ideal, while N′ is finite from the original finite list of equations; Noetherianity is not needed.

items.name: Clear one ideal-membership denominator in a localization
items.statement: For a commutative semiring R, submonoid M and localization S, algebraMap(x) belongs to the extended ideal I S if and only if some m∈M satisfies m x∈I.
items.note: Unlike an injective-localization argument this also permits zero divisors and accounts for denominators that annihilate a difference. Z40 takes the finite product of the denominators for the given generators.

items.name: A finite submersive presentation is standard smooth
items.statement: For commutative R-algebras S and finite variable and relation index types, a SubmersivePresentation R S gives IsStandardSmooth R S.
items.note: SubmersivePresentation and its unit-Jacobian field read in Extension/Presentation/Submersive.lean:492. The existing anonymous instance [IsStandardSmooth R S]→Smooth R S is read at Smooth/StandardSmoothCotangent.lean:343; it is an import, not a new named declaration. Z42 explicitly supplies the inverse-coordinate presentation.

items.name: Smoothness on a basic open
items.statement: For a finitely presented algebra B over a commutative ring A and b∈B, D(b)⊂Algebra.smoothLocus A B if and only if Localization.Away b is smooth over A.
items.note: IsSmoothAt means formal smoothness of B_p (Locus.lean:46), not finite presentation of B_p over A. This distinction is retained in Z41/Z43.

items.name: Containment of zero loci is containment in a radical
items.statement: For ideals I,K of a commutative semiring R, V(I)⊂V(K) if and only if K⊂radical(I).
items.note: Used with I=H+J and K=(v), after passing from Spec(P/J) to primes of P containing J. This needs neither Noetherianity nor a field Nullstellensatz.

items.name: Radical membership is membership of some natural power
items.statement: For an ideal I of a commutative semiring R, x∈radical(I) if and only if there is n∈N with x^n∈I.
items.note: The exponent may be zero when I is the unit ideal. It is an existence statement; no computable or presentation-independent bound is supplied.

items.name: Localizations are formally smooth
items.statement: For a commutative ring R and multiplicative submonoid M, every localization R_M is formally smooth over R.
items.note: The same source's instance at line497 composes this with formal smoothness of an ambient algebra. Together with the polynomial instance at line112 this gives formal smoothness of P_Q over the coefficient ring; no finite-presentation assertion for localization at a prime.

items.name: A square matrix with a left inverse has unit determinant
items.statement: Over a commutative ring, if finite square matrices U,V satisfy V U=1, then det(U) is a unit.
items.note: After L35 selects a basis from the columns of a split-surjective matrix, its inverse basis matrix supplies the left inverse. Applies also to the empty matrix with determinant 1.

items.name: Polynomial differential coordinates are partial derivatives
items.statement: For a commutative coefficient ring R, in the canonical basis dX_i of Ω_(R[X]/R), the i-th coordinate of df is the formal partial derivative ∂_i f.
items.note: The basis definition at line60 and evaluation formula were read. Tensoring and L45 identify the conormal map for P_Q→B_p with the original fixed Jacobian, so no change of presentation is silently substituted.

items.name: Differentials localize with the algebra
items.statement: For a tower of commutative rings R→S→T where T localizes S at M, the natural map Ω_(S/R)→Ω_(T/R) makes the latter the localized S-module.
items.note: Read the tower and IsLocalization hypotheses. The preceding tensorKaehlerEquivOfFormallyEtale and its value on d(algebraMap s) identify the localized coordinate basis.

items.name: A retract of a projective module is projective
items.statement: If i:P→M and s:M→P are R-linear with s i=id_P and M is projective, then P is projective.
items.note: Applied to the split conormal injection into the finite free module B_p^N. Free modules are projective in the immediately preceding instance.

items.name: Finite projective modules are finitely presented
items.statement: A finitely generated projective module over a commutative ring is finitely presented.
items.note: This discharges the finite-presentation hypothesis of L35 on the conormal module. Do not infer it merely from finite generation over a possibly non-Noetherian base.

items.name: Localization at one element is smooth
items.statement: For a commutative ring R and r∈R, an R-algebra which is Localization.Away r is smooth over R.
items.note: Combines formal smoothness with the finite presentation obtained by adjoining an inverse to r. Not a finite-presentation assertion for an arbitrary prime localization.

items.name: Smooth ring maps compose
items.statement: For a compatible tower of commutative algebras R→A→B, if A is smooth over R and B is smooth over A, then B is smooth over R.
items.note: Z44 applies this to S→S[1/v]→B[1/v] before invoking the S-relative basic-open smooth-locus theorem.

items.name: Finite local generation yields a global conductor witness
items.statement: Let P be a commutative ring, Q a prime, F⊂J ideals with J generated by f_1,…,f_q. If F P_Q=J P_Q, there is k∉Q with kJ⊂F.
items.locator: Adapter to Elkik §0.2, conductor K_alpha; exact localization membership supplier L37
items.note: Owner: SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4. Codex — codex-a71f92, second continuation. Explicit source-level proof adapter, no Lean implementation.

items.name: Smoothness selects original equations and a Jacobian minor
items.statement: Let A be a commutative ring, P=A[X_1,…,X_N], J=(f_1,…,f_q), B=P/J, p∈Spec B and Q its inverse-image prime in P. If B is smooth at p, there are subsets α⊂{1,…,q}, β⊂{1,…,N} of equal size such that J P_Q=F_α P_Q and δ=det(∂_(β_j) f_(α_i)) does not belong to Q.
items.locator: Fixed-presentation refinement of Elkik §0.2; Stacks 031I and 00TA proof
items.note: Owner: SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4. Codex — codex-a71f92, second continuation. Explicit source-level proof adapter, no Lean implementation.

items.name: A conductor-weighted minor gives a standard-smooth open
items.statement: In Z03 let α,β have equal size, δ the corresponding minor and k∈(F_α:J). Put h=kδ. Then B[1/h] is a standard-smooth A-algebra and hence smooth; the case of the zero localization is allowed.

items.name: The full Elkik ideal defines exactly the nonsmooth locus
items.statement: For the finite polynomial presentation and full ideal H of Z03 over any commutative A, a prime p of B=P/J is a smooth point over A if and only if the image of H is not contained in p. Equivalently the smooth locus is Spec B minus V(H B).
items.locator: Elkik §0.2, printed555/PDF4; arbitrary-base extension proved by Z40–Z42

items.name: Generic smoothness gives one universal power identity
items.statement: For a finite presentation B=P/J over a commutative ring S, v∈S, and the full H of Z03, if B[1/v] is smooth over S[1/v], then there is r≥0 with v^r∈H+J in P. In particular there are h∈H and polynomial coefficients b_i with v^r=h+Σ_i b_i f_i. The choice is made before any coefficient base change.

items.name: Invariant vectors recognized by scalar extension
items.statement: For a finite Galois extension L/K, a semilinear Galois representation V over L and a K-linear invariant map f:W→V, if L⊗_K W→V induced by f is surjective then image(f)=V^Gal(L/K). Neither W nor V need be finite-dimensional.

items.name: Purely inseparable elements have scalar powers
items.statement: For a purely inseparable field extension E/F of exponential characteristic q and x∈E, some x^(q^n) belongs to the image of F. In characteristic zero q=1.

items.name: Algebraic extensions above their separable closure are purely inseparable
items.statement: If E/F is algebraic, E is purely inseparable over the relative separable closure of F in E.

items.name: Connectedness of spectra descends along injections
items.statement: For an injective homomorphism of commutative rings R→S, connectedness of Spec S implies connectedness of Spec R. Nontriviality of R follows from that of S.

items.name: Finite-module restricted-series base change
items.statement: Let A be a complete separated nonarchimedean Noetherian Tate ring with countably generated uniformity, and M a finite A-module with its module topology and continuous addition. For k finite variables, the coefficientwise map M⊗_A A⟨X₁,…,X_k⟩→M⟨X₁,…,X_k⟩ is a linear equivalence. This is not yet an affinoid quotient algebra or completed-tensor comparison.

items.name: Tensor products of flat modules are flat
items.statement: For a commutative ring R and flat R-modules M,N, M⊗_R N is R-flat; the pinned instance also allows the first module to be flat over an R-algebra S and returns S-flatness.

items.name: Flatness is transitive
items.statement: For compatible scalar actions R→S on M, if S is R-flat and M is S-flat then M is R-flat.
items.note: Pinned declaration statements read; no new Lean implementation.

items.name: Flat modules preserve regular scalar multiplication
items.statement: If r is a non-zero-divisor of a commutative ring R and M is R-flat, multiplication by r on M is injective.
items.note: Pinned declaration statements read; no new Lean implementation.

items.name: Connected locally Noetherian schemes with domain stalks are irreducible
items.statement: A connected locally Noetherian scheme whose every local ring is a domain is irreducible. Its reducedness and the affine domain conclusion are separate consequences.
items.note: Pinned declaration statements read; no new Lean implementation.

items.name: Iteration of completed restricted series
items.statement: For a topological commutative Huber ring A and natural k,m, A⟨X₁,…,X_(k+m)⟩ and A⟨X₁,…,X_k⟩⟨Y₁,…,Y_m⟩ are canonically ring-isomorphic by mutually continuous maps preserving coefficients and the two blocks of variables. Here the series rings are Tau Ceti’s separated completed restricted series.

items.name: Smooth algebras remain smooth under base change
items.statement: For commutative R-algebras A,B, if A is smooth over R then B⊗_R A is smooth over B.

items.name: Galois norm of an idempotent in a pointed connected algebra
items.statement: Let A be a connected commutative K-algebra with a K-algebra retraction ε:A→K and L/K a finite Galois extension. Every idempotent of L⊗_K A is 0 or 1; thus its spectrum is connected. No normality, reducedness or finite-type hypothesis on A is required.

items.name: Purely inseparable base change preserves idempotents
items.statement: For any commutative K-algebra A and purely inseparable field extension L/K, the injection A→A⊗_K L induces a bijection on idempotents. In particular connectedness is preserved, including for finite extensions over an imperfect field.

items.name: Finite-extension connectedness of an augmented connected algebra
items.statement: If Spec A is connected for a commutative K-algebra A admitting a K-algebra retraction to K, then Spec(A⊗_K L) is connected for every finite field extension L/K.

items.name: Distinguished coordinates for a nonzero restricted series
items.statement: Over a complete nontrivially valued nonarchimedean field K, any finite family of nonzero elements of K⟨X₁,…,X_n⟩ (n>0) can simultaneously be made X_n-distinguished by an isometric triangular coordinate change X_i↦X_i+X_n^(t^(n−i)), i<n, X_n↦X_n, for sufficiently large integer t. Distinguished means the leading coefficient is a unit of maximal norm and all higher coefficients have strictly smaller norm.

items.name: Weierstrass division for Tate algebras
items.statement: For g∈K⟨X₁,…,X_n⟩ distinguished of degree s in X_n and f in the same algebra, there are unique q in that algebra and r∈K⟨X₁,…,X_(n−1)⟩[X_n] with degree r<s such that f=qg+r. The Gauss norms satisfy |f|=max(|q||g|,|r|). K is complete and nontrivially nonarchimedean.

items.name: Affinoid Noether normalization from distinguished division
items.statement: For a proper ideal I of the strict Tate algebra T_n(K), there exists d≤n and a finite injective K-algebra homomorphism T_d(K)→T_n(K)/I. The map need not be the original coordinate inclusion.
items.note: Source-level proof plan; no Lean implementation. Owner: AdicSpacesPartII:R0.

items.name: Finite maximal residue fields of strict affinoids
items.statement: Every maximal ideal m of a strict K-affinoid algebra A has residue field finite over K. Consequently every nonempty clopen of Spec A contains a closed point that becomes K′-rational after a finite extension K′/K; finitely many chosen points can be rationalized in one finite extension.

items.name: Strict affinoid completed tensor and quotient presentation
items.statement: For strict K-affinoids A=K⟨X⟩/I and B=K⟨Y⟩/J over a complete nontrivially valued nonarchimedean field, their completed tensor is K⟨X,Y⟩/(I,J), with its quotient Banach topology. It represents pairs of continuous K-algebra maps to a commutative Banach K-algebra. Use the existing AdicSpacesPartII:R0 carrier and prove presentation independence.

items.statement: Let O be a complete DVR with uniformizer π, K=Frac O, and B_i a finite family of finite-type O-algebras. Set C_i=π-adic completion of B_i and P=⊗_O B_i. Then C=π-adic completion of P identifies with the π-adic completed tensor of the C_i, and C[1/π]≅⊗̂_K(C_i[1/π]). These identifications preserve coefficients and factor maps.

items.name: Completion of a G-ring is a regular morphism
items.statement: If P is a Noetherian G-ring and I an ideal, then P→P̂_I is flat with geometrically regular fibers. In particular it remains a regular map after inverting any element. This does not say the completion is a G-ring.

items.name: Regularity ascends along a flat map with regular fibers
items.statement: For a flat local homomorphism R→S of Noetherian local rings, if R and S/m_R S are regular then S is regular. Consequently a regular map from a regular Noetherian ring has regular Noetherian target.

items.name: One-generic GLn tame inertia has distinct characters
items.statement: Let p be prime, f,n≥1, s=(s_j) in (S_n)^f, and μ a lowest-alcove weight that is 1-deep in every embedding. In formula (2.12), the n characters χ_i of tame inertia are pairwise distinct over a sufficiently large residue field. This is the GLn regularity assertion, with no semisimplicity assumption on an extension to G_K.

items.name: Multiplicity-free tame inertia gives semisimplicity
items.statement: Let K be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p and F a finite field of characteristic p large enough to split the finite tame inertia image of a continuous finite-dimensional representation ρ:G_K→GL(V). Suppose wild inertia acts trivially and V restricted to inertia is a sum of pairwise distinct one-dimensional characters. Then V is a direct sum of simple F[G_K]-modules, indexed by Frobenius orbits on the inertia characters. Frobenius itself need not act semisimply.

items.name: Generic tame residual representations are semisimple
items.statement: For a continuous tame representation ρ:G_K→GL_n(F), if ρ is m-generic in Definition 5.5.1 with m≥1, then ρ is semisimple. The conclusion is stable under a finite splitting-field extension and descends to F.

items.name: Genericity transfer justifies the tame admissibility argument
items.statement: Under Corollary 5.5.8, let λ_j∈[0,h]^n, let τ have an (h+1)-generic lowest-alcove presentation, and let ρ be tame with R_ρ^(λ,τ) nonzero. After a finite coefficient extension, a characteristic-zero point gives a residual Kisin lattice in Y^[0,h],τ. Corollary 5.5.10 makes ρ 1-generic; hence K47 makes ρ semisimple and Proposition 5.5.7 applies. This supplies the previously missing justification of the semisimple step.

items.name: Adequacy for polarized finite residual images
items.statement: For a finite subgroup H⊂G_n(F), let H0=H∩G_n^0(F) and let ad V=gl_n(F) with the polarized adjoint action. In Thorne Definition 2.3, H is adequate when H^0(H,ad V)=0, H^1(H0,F)=0, H^1(H,ad V)=0, and for every irreducible F[H]-submodule W⊂ad V there exist h∈H0 and an eigenvalue α of its GL_n component such that tr(e_{h,α}W)≠0; e is the projector to the full generalized α-eigenspace. Work over a finite coefficient field containing the relevant eigenvalues. This G_n definition differs from the GL_n definition using ad^0.

items.name: Trace evaluation kills the auxiliary dual Selmer group
items.statement: In the hypotheses of A14 and for a Taylor–Wiles set Q with the scalar-inertia condition A13, the augmented dual Selmer group is the kernel of H^1_{L^perp,T}(G_{F+,S},ad rbar(1))→⊕_{v∈Q}F given by c↦(tr(e_{Frob_v,α_v}c(Frob_v)))_v. items.name: Local-global compatibility at auxiliary parahoric level
items.statement: Assume the Appendix A.4 setting: p>2, F/F+ CM with F+≠Q, all p-adic places split, a unitary group definite at infinity with the chosen integral model away from N, a sufficiently small compact open U, and S containing the p-adic places, primes dividing N and all non-hyperspecial places of U. Fix a dominant algebraic weight λ, WD inertial types τ_v, a stable O-lattice W in ⊗_{v|p}σ(λ_v,τ_v)^*◦ι_v, and the nonzero localized residual Hecke eigensystem with absolutely irreducible rbar|G_F from the Appendix A setup. Fix a Taylor–Wiles datum Q disjoint from S and the associated ideal m_Q away from S∪Q. Put ξ=ε^(1−n)δ_(F/F+)^n. At p use Hodge weights λ_v+η and WD monodromy dominated by τ_v, as required by E33–E34. At U_0(Q) there is a polarized representation r(U_0(Q),W)_mQ:G_{F+,S}→G_n(T_0^pr), with the same corrected deformation datum as A17; in particular it remains unramified at Q. For each allowed split w away from S∪Q, det(1−r|G_F(Frob_w)X)=Σ_{j=0}^n(−1)^j(Nw)^(j(j−1)/2)α_level(T_w^(j))X^j. Here α_level is α_0. Here T_i^pr is the Hecke image on the projected module H_i of A30, and the local assertions use its explicit local-compatibility hypotheses. The unrestricted full-Hecke version of the printed theorem is not established by the cited argument (E38).

items.name: Auxiliary Hecke algebra must be restricted to the projector image
items.statement: In the Appendix A.4 global setting, define H_i=pr(S(U_i(Q),W)_mQ) and T_i^pr as the image of the away-from-S∪Q Hecke algebra on H_i, for i=0,1. Then the T_0^pr-valued representation is unramified at Q and the T_1^pr-valued representation has local deformation condition A13 at Q. items.name: Parahoric projector compares original-level vectors
items.statement: Let L be a local field of residue cardinality q, with residue characteristic different from the odd coefficient prime p, and q≡1 mod p. Set G=GL_n(L), K=GL_n(O_L), and let P be the standard parahoric for n=n1+n2 (1≤n2≤n). Let O be the coefficient DVR and F its residue field. Let R be a complete local O-algebra with residue F and Π a smooth R[G]-module whose compact-open invariant modules are finite free over O. For each compact open U let R_U be the image of R in End_O(Π^U). Assume Π⊗_O Qpbar is semisimple with generic irreducible constituents and every R_U[1/p] is semisimple. Assume ρ:G_L→GL_n(R_P) is continuous and, at every map R_P→Qpbar and every constituent π generated by the corresponding Π^P specialization, ρ^ss identifies with (r_p(π)^∨(1−n))^ss. Suppose ρbar is unramified and has a Frobenius eigenvalue α with full generalized eigenspace dimension n2. Form the commuting operators V^j (1≤j≤n2), the symmetric-polynomial transforms P_j of the Frobenius characteristic polynomial, and Hensel factorizations P_j=Q_j R_j where R_j mod m_R is a power of X−binom(n2,j)α^j and Q_j at that residue value is a unit. Then pr=∏_j Q_j(V^j) induces an R-linear isomorphism Π^K→pr Π^P. It is the map pr applied to original-level vectors; literal inclusion is not asserted.

items.name: Projected diamond-level representation has scalar inertia
items.statement: Let L be a local field of residue cardinality q, with residue characteristic different from the odd coefficient prime p, and q≡1 mod p. Set G=GL_n(L), K=GL_n(O_L), and let P be the standard parahoric for n=n1+n2 (1≤n2≤n). Let O be the coefficient DVR and F its residue field. Let R be a complete local O-algebra with residue F and Π a smooth R[G]-module whose compact-open invariant modules are finite free over O. For each compact open U let R_U be the image of R in End_O(Π^U). Assume Π⊗_O Qpbar is semisimple with generic irreducible constituents and every R_U[1/p] is semisimple. Let P1 be the kernel of P→GL_n2(k_L)→k_L^×→k_L^×(p). Assume ρ:G_L→GL_n(R_P1) and the same specialization compatibility as A31, using Π^P1, and let pr be its generalized-eigenspace projector. Put R′=image(R→End_O(pr Π^P1)). Then ρ⊗R′ canonically splits as s⊕ψ, lifting the complementary residual subspace and the selected full α-generalized eigenspace: s is unramified and ψ has scalar tame inertia character χ. For u∈O_L^× the diamond operator V_u on pr Π^P1 equals χ(Art_L(u)).

items.name: Diamond freeness and augmentation descent
items.statement: In the sufficiently small definite-unitary setting, let V⊂U be normal compact open subgroups equal at p and let Δ=U/V be a finite abelian p-group. For a finite free O coefficient lattice W with the prescribed action, S(V,W) is finite free over O[Δ]. The natural inclusion identifies S(U,W) with S(V,W)^Δ. The trace induces an isomorphism S(V,W)_Δ→S(U,W), so invariants and coinvariants are both identified with the base level through their respective maps. If a commuting spectral projector cuts out a direct summand, its image is also finite free over the local ring O[Δ].

items.name: Hilbert–Samuel degree equals local dimension
items.statement: For a nonzero Noetherian local ring (R,m,k) of dimension d, n↦length_R(R/m^(n+1)) eventually agrees with a nonzero rational polynomial of degree d. Consequently, for d≥1, dim_k(m^n/m^(n+1)) eventually agrees with a nonzero polynomial of degree d−1; for d=0 these graded pieces eventually vanish.

items.name: A homogeneous relation lowers polynomial-ring growth
items.statement: Let k be a field, d≥1, A=k[X1,…,Xd] with standard grading, and I a homogeneous ideal containing a nonzero homogeneous element f of degree e≥1. For n≥e, dim_k(A/I)_n ≤ binom(n+d−1,d−1)−binom(n−e+d−1,d−1). In particular its eventual Hilbert polynomial, if nonzero, has degree at most d−2 when d≥2; when d=1 the quotient has zero degree-n piece for all n≥e. If I contains a nonzero constant then I=A and all pieces vanish.

items.name: Associated graded algebra of a regular local ring
